Benchmark.title: Apple macOS 15 (Sequoia) Security Technical Implementation Guide (SAMPLE EXCERPT)

Rule.title: The macOS system must enforce screen saver password.
Rule.description: <VulnDiscussion>Users must authenticate when unlocking the screen saver. The screen saver acts as a session lock and prevents unauthorized users from accessing the current user's account.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><Mitigations></Mitigations>
Rule.fixtext: Install the "com.apple.screensaver" configuration profile to enable a password prompt when unlocking the screen saver. (Sample text — see official STIG.)

check.check-content:
Verify the macOS system requires a password to unlock the screen saver:
/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript << EOS $.NSUserDefaults.alloc.initWithSuiteName('com.apple.screensaver')\ .objectForKey('askForPassword').js EOS
If the result is not "true", this is a finding. (Sample text — see official STIG.)

Rule.title: The macOS system must limit consecutive failed login attempts to three.
Rule.description: <VulnDiscussion>The macOS system must be configured to limit the number of failed login attempts to a maximum of three. When the maximum number of failed attempts is reached, the account must be locked for a period of time. This protects against brute-force attacks that attempt to gain unauthorized access.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives>
Rule.fixtext: Install the "com.apple.mobiledevice.passwordpolicy" configuration profile to enforce a maximum of three consecutive failed login attempts. (Sample text — see official STIG.)

check.check-content:
Verify the macOS system limits consecutive failed login attempts:
/usr/bin/pwpolicy getaccountpolicies | tail -n +2 | /usr/bin/xmllint --xpath '//dict/key[text()="policyAttributeMaximumFailedAuthentications"]/following-sibling::integer[1]/text()' -
If the result is not 3 or lower, this is a finding. (Sample text — see official STIG.)

Rule.title: The macOS system must prevent Apple Watch from terminating a session lock.
Rule.description: <VulnDiscussion>Session locks must only be terminated by re-authentication with an authorized credential. Allowing an Apple Watch to unlock the system weakens the session lock. (Sample text.)</VulnDiscussion>
Rule.fixtext: Install a configuration profile that disables Apple Watch auto-unlock. (Sample text — see official STIG.)

check.check-content: Verify auto-unlock with Apple Watch is disabled. If enabled, this is a finding. (Sample text — see official STIG.)

Rule.title: The macOS system must automatically remove or disable temporary user accounts after 72 hours.
Rule.description: <VulnDiscussion>Temporary accounts left active beyond their intended lifetime provide an avenue for unauthorized access. They must be removed or disabled within 72 hours. (Sample text.)</VulnDiscussion>
Rule.fixtext: Remove or disable temporary accounts within 72 hours of creation. (Sample text — see official STIG.)

check.check-content: Ask the administrator if temporary accounts are used. If they persist beyond 72 hours, this is a finding. (Sample text — see official STIG.)

Rule.title: The macOS system must enforce time synchronization.
Rule.description: <VulnDiscussion>Accurate time is required for audit record correlation and authentication protocols. The system must synchronize with an authoritative time source. (Sample text.)</VulnDiscussion>
Rule.fixtext: Enable time synchronization: /usr/bin/sudo /usr/sbin/systemsetup -setusingnetworktime on (Sample text — see official STIG.)

check.check-content: Verify network time is enabled: /usr/sbin/systemsetup -getusingnetworktime If "Network Time: On" is not returned, this is a finding. (Sample text — see official STIG.)

Rule.title: The macOS system must disable hot corners.
Rule.description: <VulnDiscussion>A hot corner can be configured to disable the screen saver, bypassing the session lock. Hot corners must be disabled. (Sample text; severity illustrative.)</VulnDiscussion>
Rule.fixtext: Install a configuration profile that disables hot corners. (Sample text — see official STIG.)

check.check-content: Verify hot corners are disabled via profiles output. If any wvous-*-corner returns a disabling value, this is a finding. (Sample text — see official STIG.)
